title: Petroglyphs of Saimaluu Tash
description: Bronze Age herders begin pecking thousands of images into the rocks of a mountain gallery, one of the largest petroglyph collections in the world.

title: Karakhanid power rises at Balasagun
description: In the confusion after the fall of the Uyghur Khaganate a Karluk-led dynasty forms at Balasagun, whose later rulers convert to Islam and whose ruined minaret, the Burana Tower, still stands.

title: Mongols subdue the Kyrgyz
description: Genghis Khan's son Jochi marches north and subdues the Kyrgyz and other forest peoples of the Yenisei, who then still lived far from their modern homeland.

title: Kyrgyz Khaganate defeats the Uyghurs
description: The Kyrgyz Khaganate destroys the Uyghur Khaganate, reaches its greatest extent and the Kyrgyz begin moving from the Yenisei toward the Tian Shan.

title: Dzungar overlordship
description: The Dzungar Khanate under Galdan extends its rule over the Tian Shan, and the Kyrgyz pay tribute to the Oirat khans for most of a century.

title: Kokand builds Pishpek
description: The Khanate of Kokand builds a mud-brick fort at Pishpek to command the northern nomads and the caravan road, the seed of modern Bishkek.

title: Ormon Khan unites the northern Kyrgyz
description: Ormon of the Sarybagysh is proclaimed khan of the northern Kyrgyz and skillfully balances between Kokand, Russia and the Kazakh khans.

title: Russians take Pishpek and Tokmok
description: Russian columns storm and raze the Kokand forts of Tokmok and Pishpek, beginning the annexation of the Kyrgyz lands.

title: Kara-Kirghiz Autonomous Oblast
description: Soviet national delimitation gives the Kyrgyz their own region within the Russian republic, the first trace of a Kyrgyz state.

title: Kirghiz ASSR
description: The region is raised to an autonomous republic, and Pishpek is renamed Frunze after the Bolshevik commander born there.

title: Kirghiz SSR
description: Kirghizia becomes a full union republic of the Soviet Union, on the borders the country kept in 1991.

title: Osh riots
description: A dispute over housing land explodes into clashes between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks in the Fergana Valley, killing hundreds.

title: Akayev elected president
description: The republic's parliament chooses physicist Askar Akayev as president, a compromise candidate who turns into the region's most liberal ruler.

title: Independence
description: Kyrgyzstan declares independence from the collapsing Soviet Union.

title: Som introduced
description: Kyrgyzstan is the first Central Asian state to leave the rouble zone and issue its own currency.

title: Manas millennium
description: Kyrgyzstan celebrates the thousandth anniversary of the epic of Manas, the centrepiece of national identity.

title: Batken incursions
description: Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan fighters cross from Tajikistan into the Batken region and take hostages, and return the following summer.

title: Manas air base
description: The United States opens a transit centre at the capital's airport for the war in Afghanistan; it stays until 2014 even as Russia keeps its own base nearby.

title: Tulip Revolution
description: Protests over a rigged election storm the government quarter and President Akayev flees to Russia, the first of the post-Soviet colour revolutions to reach Central Asia.

title: Bakiyev elected president
description: Kurmanbek Bakiyev wins a landslide to succeed Akayev, and rules until he is overthrown in turn.

title: Revolution of 2010
description: Security forces fire on crowds outside the White House and the killing turns a protest into a revolution; President Bakiyev flees the capital and then the country.

title: Osh ethnic clashes
description: Riots between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks burn out districts of Osh and Jalal-Abad and kill hundreds, mostly Uzbeks.

title: Parliamentary constitution
description: A referendum approved under interim president Roza Otunbayeva turns Kyrgyzstan from a presidential into a parliamentary republic.

title: First World Nomad Games
description: Athletes from forty countries compete in horseback wrestling, eagle hunting and other nomad sports beside Issyk-Kul.

title: Jeenbekov elected president
description: Sooronbay Jeenbekov succeeds the term-limited Almazbek Atambayev, Central Asia's first peaceful transfer of power between elected presidents.
